candidate_contribution_statement: An end-to-end, falsifiable protocol for testing whether a pre-target frozen exact bit witness contains information about a later certified random target, while explicitly controlling freeze-time side information, causal common causes, optional stopping, rollback/fork attacks, candidate multiplicity, and external evidence continuity.

closest_prior_art.area: Future random target guessed after response
closest_prior_art.delta: These paradigms randomize a future target after the guess and use strong transparency/replication methods, but do not use certified public post-freeze randomness, exact 256-bit identity, explicit conditional-min-entropy relative to the complete freeze-time view, anytime-valid e-process evidence, or rollback/BFT continuity as one composed protocol.
examples: D. J. Bem, Feeling the Future, JPSP 2011, DOI 10.1037/a0021524
Kekecs et al., Transparent Psi Project, Royal Society Open Science 2023
Walleczek et al., PLOS ONE 2025, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0335330

closest_prior_art.area: Commit now, use future public randomness
closest_prior_art.delta: NIST provides the future-randomness/precommit primitive, not a causal-anomaly test of whether the future value was already encoded in a frozen earlier witness.
examples: NIST Interoperable Randomness Beacons applications: commit upfront, derive later randomness from a future pulse

closest_prior_art.delta: These works certify/trace unpredictability and side-information bounds; they do not test pre-existing exact predictions of their later outputs.
examples: Bierhorst et al., Nature 2018, Experimentally Generated Randomness Certified by the Impossibility of Superluminal Signals
Kavuri et al., Nature 2025, Traceable random numbers from a non-local quantum advantage

closest_prior_art.delta: These works model or characterize retrocausal channels/CTCs. AIFC instead targets the empirical evidence problem: how to reject an ordinary forward-causal null without assuming a CTC channel exists.
examples: Lloyd et al., PRL 2011, Closed Timelike Curves via Postselection
Ji, Lloyd, Wilde, PRL 2026, Retrocausal Capacity of a Quantum Channel

closest_prior_art.delta: AIFC applies these tools to exact post-freeze target identity with history-wise guessing caps.
examples: e-values/e-processes and valid sequential inference literature

closest_prior_art.delta: AIFC makes the complete pre-target transcript and latent/shared-state audit an explicit evidence gate for future-information claims.
examples: Bell/device-independent randomness literature on side information and measurement independence

closest_prior_art.area: Tamper-evident logging, rollback/fork protection, quorum intersection
closest_prior_art.delta: AIFC imports these as temporal-evidence continuity requirements so an apparently early prediction cannot be manufactured by rollback, replay or split history.
On-chain timestamping addresses immutability/provenance but not certified future randomness, conditional entropy, causal isolation, anytime-valid inference and full evidence-stack soundness.

recommended_paper_positioning: Methodology / foundations / scientific inference paper. Claim a protocol and soundness theorem under stated assumptions, not discovery of retrocausality.
review_scope: Targeted literature/web prior-art sweep for the combined operational protocol, not an exhaustive patent/legal novelty search.

empty_cross_domain_queries: future random + hash chain + prediction protocol
search_result.interpretation: No exact prior-art match was found in the targeted corpus. Absence from this search is not proof of global novelty.

strongest_defensible_claim_now: Candidate methodological novelty: a compositional, fail-closed evidence stack for testing pre-existing information about certified post-freeze random targets. Scientific novelty is plausible from this sweep but not yet established by exhaustive scholarly/patent review or peer review.
working_title: Auditable Tests for Information from Future Random Events: A Causal, Cryptographic, and Anytime-Valid Protocol
